selected_modules.reason: The failures are compile-time diagnostics in C++ tests about compound literals/temporary arrays ("taking address of temporary array"). The issue summary is specifically a g++ regression, and reproducer cases include g++.dg tests under C++17 and ext/compound-literal coverage. That points first to C++ front-end semantic handling of compound literals, array prvalues, temporaries, and address-taking rules.

One reproducer is a C test (c-c++-common/array-lit.c) with a dangling-pointer warning expectation involving array literals/temporaries. Even though the observed C failure is a parse/diagnostic mismatch, compound literals are fundamentally C-front-end territory, so C semantics and parsing of array literals/compound literals are directly relevant to the shared regression surface.

The observed behavior is entirely before optimization passes (all logged as compile_error_before_passes despite pass availability), and the reproducer expectations are warnings/diagnostics about temporary arrays and dangling pointers across both C and C++. Shared C-family code is a strong candidate for common diagnostics, warning logic, and front-end helper semantics used by both gcc/c and gcc/cp.

Compound literals and temporary objects ultimately rely on GCC’s core tree representation and generic tree-level semantics/lowering. Because the bug spans both C and C++ tests around arrays/temporaries rather than backend codegen, tree-core is a plausible shared intermediate layer underneath the front ends, more so than optimizer or target modules.
